services.title: Professional data training
services.summary: Structured, practical programs that take beginners and working professionals from foundational skills to job-ready data work.
services.body:
Data skills are the foundation of every data-driven organisation. Our training programs are cohort-based and project-driven: participants learn by working on realistic datasets and business questions, not by watching slides.

## How the training works
Each cohort follows a structured curriculum with clear milestones. Sessions combine short concept introductions with hands-on practice, peer review and mentor feedback, so participants leave with a portfolio of work rather than a certificate alone.

## Who it is for
- Graduates and career changers building a pathway into data roles
- Working professionals who need practical analysis skills alongside their job
- Teams that want a shared foundation in working with data
features: Data Talents Program: Data Analysis, Data Engineering and other specializations
outcomes: A portfolio of real analysis projects
Confidence working with real business data

services.title: Corporate team upskilling
services.summary: Tailored data training for your staff, designed around your tools, your data and the decisions your teams make every day.
services.body:
Generic courses rarely change how a team works. We design training around your organisation: the systems you already use, the reports your managers rely on, and the questions your teams need to answer.

## Our approach
We start by understanding current skill levels and the decisions that matter most. The program is then built around your own (anonymised where needed) data, so every exercise is directly relevant to day-to-day work.

## Formats
- Short intensive workshops for specific skills
- Multi-week programs for deeper capability building
- Data literacy sessions for managers and leadership
features: Curriculum built on your own data and tools
Workshops, multi-week programs or leadership sessions
outcomes: Teams that can answer their own data questions
Less dependence on a few specialists

services.title: Data products for companies
services.summary: Dashboards, reports and analytical tools that put the right numbers in front of the right people at the right time.
services.body:
A data product turns raw information into something people use every day: a dashboard a manager checks each morning, an automated report, or a model that flags what needs attention.

## What we build
We design and build data products around a specific decision or workflow. Every product is scoped with the people who will use it, tested against real data, and documented so your team can maintain it.

## How we keep it useful
- We define the decisions the product should support before building anything
- We validate data quality at the source, so numbers can be trusted
- We hand over with training and documentation

services.title: Data-driven systems & internal tools
services.summary: Systems and internal tools that capture clean data from day one and connect it to the processes that run your business.
services.body:
Good analysis depends on good data, and good data depends on the systems that capture it. We build internal tools, integrations and data pipelines that make reliable data a by-product of everyday work.

## Typical engagements
- Data pipelines that bring together information from several systems
- Internal tools that replace spreadsheets and paper forms
- Integrations between existing business applications
- Data warehouses that support reporting and analytics

Every system is designed with data protection, access control and maintainability in mind.
outcomes: A foundation that scales with you

services.title: Business digitization
services.summary: Moving manual, paper-based and spreadsheet processes into digital systems, so your business can see and use its own data.
services.body:
Many businesses still run on paper records, notebooks and disconnected spreadsheets. That information is valuable, but hard to use. We help organisations across sectors digitize their processes step by step.

## How we approach digitization
We map how work happens today, identify where data is created and lost, and introduce digital tools in phases so teams can adapt without disruption.

## What changes
- Records become searchable and consistent
- Managers get visibility without chasing updates
- Data starts to accumulate in a form that can be analysed
features: Data migration from paper and spreadsheets

services.title: Data strategy development
services.summary: A clear, practical roadmap that connects your data investments to business priorities, people and governance.
services.body:
A data strategy answers simple questions that are hard to get right: which decisions matter most, what data supports them, who is responsible, and what to build first.

## What a strategy engagement covers
- Assessment of current data maturity, systems and skills
- Prioritised use cases tied to business objectives
- Governance: ownership, quality standards and access
- A phased roadmap with realistic investment and capability plans

We keep strategies practical. The output is a plan your team can act on, not a document that sits on a shelf.
outcomes: Alignment between leadership and data teams
Investment focused on the highest-value work

services.title: Research, development & data collection
services.summary: Rigorous research design, field data collection and analysis that produce evidence you can rely on.
services.body:
Sometimes the data you need does not exist yet. We design and run research and data collection exercises, from survey design to fieldwork and final analysis.

## Our research services
- Research and survey design
- Digital field data collection with quality controls
- Data cleaning, analysis and reporting
- Monitoring and evaluation frameworks

We apply consent, privacy and data minimisation principles throughout, so research is both rigorous and responsible.

services.title: Data protection compliance
services.summary: Practical guidance to help your organisation handle personal data lawfully and responsibly, and stay compliant as you grow.
services.body:
Data protection is now a legal requirement as well as a matter of trust. In Rwanda, Law No. 058/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy sets clear obligations for organisations that collect and process personal data.

## How we help
- Data mapping: what personal data you hold, where, and why
- Gap assessments against legal requirements
- Policies, notices and consent processes
- Guidance on registration, data subject rights and breach response
- Staff awareness training

We focus on compliance that works in practice and fits how your organisation actually operates.
outcomes: A clear picture of your obligations
Greater trust from customers and partners

Built for professionals who want to use data better in their current role. The program covers the analysis skills that make an immediate difference at work, taught on a schedule that fits around a full-time job.

posts.title: What being data driven actually means for a growing business
posts.excerpt: Being data driven is less about technology and more about habits: asking better questions, trusting a shared set of numbers, and acting on evidence.
posts.body:
Many organisations want to become "data driven", but the phrase is often treated as a technology purchase. In practice, it is a set of habits.

## Start with decisions, not data
The most useful question is not "what data do we have?" but "which decisions do we make repeatedly, and what would help us make them better?" A clear list of decisions gives every data investment a purpose.

## Agree on one version of the numbers
When finance, sales and operations each keep their own figures, meetings turn into debates about whose spreadsheet is right. Agreeing on shared definitions for key metrics is one of the highest-value steps an organisation can take.

## Build skills alongside systems
Dashboards only help if people can read and question them. Investing in data literacy across teams makes every system you build more useful.

## Take small, visible steps
Pick one decision, improve the data behind it, and show the result. Early wins build the trust needed for larger changes.

posts.title: Data protection basics every Rwandan organisation should know
posts.excerpt: Rwanda's data protection law applies to any organisation handling personal data. Here are the practical first steps to take.
posts.body:
Law No. 058/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy sets out how organisations in Rwanda must collect, use and protect personal data. Compliance can feel daunting, but the first steps are practical.

## Know what personal data you hold
Start with a simple inventory: what personal data do you collect, where is it stored, who can access it, and why do you need it?

## Be transparent
People should understand what you collect and why. Clear privacy notices and consent processes are a foundation of compliance.

## Collect only what you need
Data minimisation reduces risk. If you do not need a piece of information, do not collect it.

## Prepare for requests and incidents
Have a process for responding to people who ask to see or correct their data, and a plan for what to do if a breach occurs.

This article is general guidance, not legal advice. For an assessment of your organisation, talk to our compliance team.

posts.title: From spreadsheets to systems: when is it time to move on?
posts.excerpt: Spreadsheets are a great starting point, but they have limits. These signs show it may be time for a more structured system.
posts.body:
Almost every business starts with spreadsheets, and for good reason: they are flexible, familiar and cheap. But as a business grows, the same flexibility becomes a risk.

## Signs you have outgrown spreadsheets
- Several versions of the same file circulate by email
- Reports take days to compile each month
- Errors are discovered after decisions have been made
- Only one person really understands how the file works

## What a better system looks like
A good system captures data once, validates it at entry, and makes it available to everyone who needs it, with the right permissions.

## Moving gradually
Digitization does not have to happen all at once. Start with the process that causes the most pain, prove the value, and expand from there.
